english: It's not truth or falsehood that matters- it's the content! The message! It's-
Va i alla hêlveten... the dwarf mutters to himself, noticing you approach.
Mr. Cityman.
Am I interrupting something?
I've got your special ink here.
Newspapers bring nothing but friction.
Great. Thanks.
The girl rolls her eyes.
She takes a step towards you and quickly grabs the set of ink cartridges.
Look, Alfoz. The Cleric just allowed us to reach the entire city.
She holds up the paper to his rocky face. "They need to hear this."
I got access to the Warehouse. It was pretty hard, I had to-
Do you know how much the Palace would love to see an article like that?
Do not put me in a position where I have to tell the Foremen to denounce the Chant!
Fore-folk.
Bah!
Step in. Solving this conflict will be a good finish to this fetch quest.
I feel like I need to step in here.
You guys seem to have a good handle on this.
Maybe I should go. (Fail to do so.)
Do you now?! the dwarf growls.
He then takes a deep breath, rubbing his eyes.
I apologize. We're having an issue.
I'm used to it.
I'm just trying to- he mutters.
Mr. Cityman. Please, enlighten us. What does the law say on criminal incitement? Specifically in print media?
It's a maze of rules. Few of them well-written.
Practically it's always an 'it depends'.
Just thinking about it makes your head hurt.
Give me a practical example.
You think I know the law?
Depends on who enforces it. And who gets enforced.
Generally I don't think the city would be very happy about it.
I'm sure they'd be fine with it.
As in, what if someone printed a newspaper calling for a violent uprising?
He groans. "One would hope!"
Ah. Then I suppose that gray zone would be a wonderful place to die.
See?
He scoffs. "You're sure about that?"
Look, Alfoz. Look at where we are!
I'm in a closet, with this god damn esoteric mess of a machine blowing hot air up my ass!
The city already guts us at every turn. The protests at the Towers. Your PPG problem.
That bullshit with the Silker's Guild!
They will never work with us. Now's our only chance. We have the people's attention.
It's time to drill it into their heads that they have the power here.
You're missing the entire picture, girl!
It's belittling to call her a girl like that.
She's clearly being unreasonable.
Bah!
He crosses his arms. "You're correct. The people have power here."
And we will use that power responsibly. By creating lasting, lawful change.
If you keep writing about violent revolution, the average person will think you're crazy.
And even worse if you push for all this other socio-relation crap!
Crap?
What, is feminism also just an ignorant reworking of Azgal's ideals?
No, it's-
The dwarf takes a deep breath. "You know I am very much in favor for pressing down hierarchies. But to put such a threatening stance on the way people have lived for centuries..."
It's not wise.
It's not wise to tell women and oppressed minorities that they should have rights?
They have rights. We have universal suffrage! Norvik is the most egalitarian city on the Coast. We've spent decades working for that.

Universal suffrage. Sure. But nine out of ten guild leaders and business owners are human men. She taps her fingers to list off her talking points. "Women earn lower salaries across all work sectors. Citizenship is withheld from Othered folktypes, on the basis of so-called 'monstrous' traits. Halflings are constantly extradited to the Horde, while every major faction ignores their pleas. Mind-control being used - somehow - as a legal tool of the state!"

And despite the outcalls, over and over again, NONE of the fore-folk have even BEGUN to address any of our core demands. And don't even get me started on rights among MGIs, or the femme-beard debacle, or your refusal to stand by all of our:
She taps her index finger against his chest with every word.
Cross.
Folk.
Attraction.
COUPLES!
(Stare at them both.)
We have toiled, Modissa, he mutters, his voice weak and dry. "Decades of work. All to reach this point."
You'll throw it all away, if you try to play their game!
You know the party is not behind even half of these ideas.
The party doesn't have vision! That's why we're not winning!
We have as many voters as the Freestriders. Potential for more.
You think the numbers matter? After all you've seen?! They don't care!
We will make them care!
The dwarf takes a step back to catch his breath.
All the other workers in the apartment just seem to go along as per usual.
This must be a common occurrence.
Do they not hear the commotion?
All this over a single article?
(Take a step away with Alfoz.) "Explain."
(Go to Modissa.) "Tell me what's going on."
Figure out why Modissa really won't tone it down.
M-I'll have to make a choice here, won't I?
Yes! they say in unison.
It's...
He appears to calm down and shakes his head. "She's bright, but she's in over her head here."
If she prints that article in the election issue, I'm certain there will be fallout.
And... it's not just that I have to deal with personally. I'm fine with that. It's my job.
But if she pushes the Chant too far from the party line...
We'll have to distance ourselves. Officially.
That's not good.
Would this article really do that much harm?
Interesting.
No. It would not be.
I'm sure of it. We already get criticized for various incidents and Azgal Youth protests.
We're toeing a line here. Carefully.
I won't allow that to be printed. I can't.
An article. That's it.
She holds it up.
It's a test page. To see the article in action before putting in the issue.
(Skim the article.)
You can't print something like this.
This is a good message. It's what the city needs.
Can't you just be a little more subtle? Or something?
'WE BUILT THIS CITY' is the name.
It's an emotional and moving Page Op about recent events, and the future of the Workers' Party.
The author weaves in arguments about city corruption with a call to action.
A direct call for the workers of the city to not let the Freestriders corrupt Norvik into becoming another oppressive 'Free City'.
Where wealth is consolidated into the hands of the few, while the many struggle to survive.

Then it gives a list of, what almost looks like demands, on several wide-ranging important topics, from the Golden Line and guild union membership fees, to social acceptance of cross-folk relations and more.
It also contains a striking subtext about wealth being extracted from the city, and sent east.
Yep. This would work on many in the city.
This does sound quite bad for the city.
Her arguments are flawed, but rooted in truth.
Clearly. She gives a mocking laugh and glares at Alfoz.
I agree.
Too bad my 'captain' over there doesn't agree. She gives a mocking laugh and glares at Alfoz.
We're past subtlety.
The people need to know that Norvik is theirs for the taking.
Come on. Help me out here, will you?
What, you want me to cast a spell on him?
No! Gods, no.
I mean... it wouldn't work, would it?
For a few minutes, maybe? But... no.
Not really, no.
She mutters a swear under her breath.
The dwarven word for hells.
She hates them.
She hates how she's been pushed down by them all her life.
She hates how powerless she feels, all the time. Every day.
Every time she walks down the street and someone looks at her funny. Every time someone asks when she's going to grow up and start a family, instead of playing around in some Azgalist larp outfit.
You see it in her eyes.
Hate and anger. Anger from endless systematic injustice.
What are you looking at? she says with a scoff.
It's your choice.
You don't need this article, Modissa. The system is unfair, yes. But don't trust Alfoz to change it. Change it yourself.
You're on the right track. Keep it up. (Give her a thumbs up.)
She stares at you.
If you publish this, they'll push you out. And everyone like you. Your voices will be silenced in the years to come. Instead, speak out slowly, bit by bit, until your ideas are accepted as the truth.
She clicks her tongue and looks over to Alfoz with frown.
Then she glares at you.
Not today. But tomorrow. And tomorrow. And tomorrow.
I know. But tell that to him.
Maybe you shouldn't. Alfoz is a very scary man.
No.
Her eyes are so filled with rage and hate.
You dare not dive deeper.
What? What are you looking at?
Stop staring. Just leave if you're not going to help.
Gods, she's a pain in the ass.
Clearly it's because of the stick up hers.
Yes you will.
Alfoz crosses his arms, looking to you both with intense stubbornness in his eyes.
Modissa grunts something to herself and adjusts her uniform.
You know Modissa is correct. You need to fight against oppression.
Perhaps she does not know what she has to, in order to convince people.
Alfoz has a more balanced view. Urthfolk will not follow some radical feminine, hyper-egalitarian dream. It's just not feasible.
Both of them are dumb. Just let them squabble.
If you side with Alfoz, he obviously has more power here - so that could help you in the future.
THE GIRL SPEAKS OF FUTURE STRINGS.
It's a fairly well-written article, but none of that matters.
This is an emotional argument, mostly. All propaganda is.
Thus, it's very, very silly.
I agree with Modissa.
I agree with Alfoz. You should not print that.
I'll leave this up to you.
You do?
He does?
Hm. Don't blame you.
Well then, Mr. Cityman.
Alfoz puffs up his chest and stares up at you.
It appears I'll have to convince you as well of how much of a mistake you're making.
You've got this, Cleric, Snell whispers to you.
Be more stubborn than the dwarf.
(Raise your arms.) "Actually- I'll just leave it up to you guys."
He steps in front of you. His face rocky stone.
You... are...
ROCK HARD.
Please, don't.
(Look down on him.)
He looks at you.
You look at him.
You make him know.
You are the KING.
Alfoz.
You... cannot...
(Try to look down on him.)
He is physically smaller.
Yet...
In soul, he is KING.
(Nod.) "...Okay. I won't intervene."
Modissa glares at you.
You're playing with fire here, Cleric.
You'll get in legal trouble for sure.
The city will turn on you, even more.
Listen to Alfoz. He knows.
The foreman gives the younger Azgal a sad expression as she lowers her head.
You know what?
Then I'm saying: it's final.
Modissa, you have to change the article. I won't tell you to gut it- I simply need you to compromise here.
I'll change it. I'll rewrite the article.
Thank you, the dwarf says and closes his eyes.
He looks extremely relieved.
But I'm not happy about it.
I am sorry. But really- thank you, Modissa.
...Mr. Cityman.
You know you must let her do her thing.
Guh...
He is sweating.
What are you two doing?
He... ugh...
He is grunting.
The Azgal Youth must be made free.
Ugh...
He groans and kneels before you.
Damn it.
Modissa is looking at you both like you're alien aberrations.
I know. It will be a massive pain in my ass, but I know.
He stands up, then throws a stern gaze at Modissa.
Print your article, girl!
Speak from your heart. And make the whole city hear you!
She smiles.
Perhaps the first time ever, in history.
A union of thoughts.
You HELD.
Garz Rubren would be proud, Alfoz.
Thank you, Alfoz.
Bah. Time will tell.
Yeah. Thanks.
I'll change the damn article.
I know this is painful, but it's simply reality. I swear.
Garz Rubren would be proud. Thank you, Modissa, he says and turns away from you.
(Whisper to her.) "Print it anyway."
Good. Good.
Huh?
Don't change it, and just print it anyway. He probably won't notice until it's too late.
Her eyes gleam.
With pure mischievous energy.
Maybe I'll do that, Mr. Cleric, she whispers back.
Maybe.
Alfoz goes over to his comrades to begin the final process on the machines.
She grunts out, "You had the ink, right?"
Mr. Cleric?
(Hand her the ink.)
She quickly looks it over with a stern face.
Red? Really?
Green? Really?
Yellow? Really?
They didn't have any black.
Well, shit.
I'll mix it out with what we have- should make it readable still.
Green is at least... thematically relevant.
She shrugs.
Even if it'll look like we're trying to lean into some fascist branding...
She shudders.
Even if it'll be hard-to-read and... a bit too Freestridery for my taste.
Maybe they'll just think it's ironic.
Then Modissa pours it into the machine.
Thanks for this. We'll actually be able to reach that last portion of voters before the election now.
She sighs. "And sorry for the mess. I shouldn't apologize, really. But..."
Her voice trails off as she stares at the components on the printer.
It's an ideological battlefield. Keep fighting.
You should chill. Nobody likes a complainer.
This is your struggle. I have no part.
She closes her eyes slowly, as if a painful headache just crept up on her.
When a woman wants to see change, she's a complainer.
When a man wants to see change, he's a hero.
That's not true.
There's some truth in that, yeah.
You're right. I should rethink my perspective.
No. You'd be just as annoying if you were a man.
She doesn't respond.
E-I should go.
That uniform seems to beg to differ.
She keeps working on the machine.
Loved that place.
Not because it was good. But lots of memories there.
So you spent a lot of time there?
You were friends with the owner?
Go on.
Oh yes. We held Youth Azgal meetings there once a week.
Oh gods, no. Mr. Drummer just served tea. We didn't talk to him much.
Really sad to see it gone.
I don't know what kind of trouble he ended up in, but I never expected Mr. Drummer to get into explosive trouble.
She is not hiding anything from you.
Tell me about this non-explosive trouble Drummer got into.
Anything else?
Her body twitches. She looks to Alfoz.
It's a point of contention. Rumors, really.
I like rumors.
Go on.
Mr. Drummer might have had some type of deal with... someone. He had people come and go at strange times.
So we could only book the shop for our meetings at specific times.
...Look. I didn't notice anything that weird. It was just...
The HWBT? she says and glances at your companion.
The HWBT?
Or the Freestriders? Maybe he had a deal or something.
...But that's rumors. Nothing else.
Nothing else?
Not really.
He just served tea, and made that clacking sound.
Alfoz might know more.
The dwarf glances over to you with a frown.
Alright.
Her eyes go wide.
She...
We talked to her once or twice. Nice gal.
We...
She shuts her mouth and points to Alfoz.
Talk to him.
No, you tell me more. Right now.
(Nod.)
Nuh-uh.
Did she just nuh-uh you?
Holy shit.
She points to Alfoz again. "I'm not a snitch. He'll tell you what you're allowed to know."
Good. Anything else?
Then she looks to the large Azgal banner hanging on the wall.
Are you kidding?
Never.
I'm just asking.
I'm voting green.
Mm. Interesting. Do you want to know what I'm voting?
(Let your lower lip quiver.)
Yeah. You want anything else?
Damn it!
She's smarter than she looks.
But can't you ask me what I'm voting for? Just for fun?
I asked you. You ask me? Please?
Yeah. Sure. Whatever. (Sulk.)
No. Anything else?
Why don't you name yourself in the paper?
What made you join the Azgal Youth?
Where are you from?
How did you get this massive printer?
Alright. No more, uh, personal questions?
It's an illegal paper, Cleric.
Ah. I see.
Been there, done there. And so on.
Been- I- it's... I... you know. It's... (Stop talking.)
She looks at you for a second, then shrugs.
Lots of things. I read Azgal for one.
The original sin.
Some great works of political literature.
I also saw the socio-economic imbalance in Norvikian society growing up, and felt like I had to do something about it. You know?
Oh, and I found a great mentor in Myran.
...Myran?
Yeah. She was the founder of the Youth Azgals. She taught me a ton.
I've heard about her. Real troublemaker.
Trouble is just another word for change.
Suppose that's true.
Myran.
That was a long time ago.
Grew up in Housing, like everyone else it seems.
Though my parents fled Reeds before I was born. The so-called Revolution was a hard time for them.
She looks a bit sad, and wanting to change the subject.
What about you?
I grew up in the Hills.
None of your business, girl.
The Hills. Then on North Wall.
You ask me, but I can't ask you?
That's how it works.
I ask the questions here.
Are you calling me a hypocrite?
Well, that's unfair.
Get better questions then.
...I don't want to argue with you.
I have some other questions.
She glares at you.
You're a farmboy?
Guess I could see that. As long as you vote green.
Hand-me-down.
She gives you a grin.
I won't tell you more than that, copper.
Even ignoring the ethical concerns with the production farms - which I won't - then it's still no.
Yeah. Don't even try sell the milk to her.
Keep the milk. The milk is YOURS.
I see. You have a weak constitution.
Nevermind then.
'Scorned' would be a good description of the expression she's giving you.
Sure?
She gives you a confounded - frankly disgusted - look.
